sections.h2: How does selling a house in Mulberry, GA work?
sections.html:
A Mulberry homeowner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from an investor, and the first job is to confirm which government answers for the parcel. Mulberry is one of Georgia's newest cities, and some addresses nearby still sit under Gwinnett County alone. Settle that before you book repairs, because it decides who issues permits and who takes code complaints.

The Census Bureau puts Mulberry at 41,445 residents on July 1, 2025, a 5.0% rise from its April 2020 base of 39,468. Gwinnett County's own fact sheet, written while the charter was still a bill in the legislature, described the city as the 17th in the county and the largest by land area. For pricing, ask a local agent for recent sold homes on your street, since a single citywide number hides a lot.

sections.h2: Is my house inside the City of Mulberry?
sections.html:
The quickest check is the city's own "Am I in Mulberry?" web app, and staff at 770-341-9640 will confirm by address or parcel number. Gwinnett County's planning notice says that since January 1, 2025 the city has been responsible for the following inside its limits:

  • Planning, zoning and rezonings, special use permits and variances
  • Code enforcement and zoning certifications
  • Building permits, development permits, sign permits and certificates of occupancy
  • Occupation tax certificates, alcohol licenses and business excise taxes

Gwinnett County keeps plan review and inspections for fire, water and sewer. The same notice adds that litigation over the Mulberry charter is pending in the Georgia Court of Appeals and in Fulton Superior Court, and that the guidance can change with the outcome. Keep any permit paperwork for the house together in one folder.

sections.h2: What zoning and permit rules should a Mulberry seller know?
sections.html:
Mulberry adopted its own zoning map on July 16, 2026, so a zoning label you remember from the county era may have changed. The city's One Map web app shows the current zoning layer, and Planning and Development staff can read it back to you by parcel number.

Buyers and their inspectors tend to ask about the same items, and the city's FAQ answers most of them:

  • Building permits are filed through the SagesGov portal and lapse after six months of inactivity.
  • An inspection is required within six months of a permit being issued, and requests go in by 4:00 PM at least two business days ahead.
  • Starting work without a required permit can bring stop work orders and fines, and the city says unauthorized work may eventually have to come out.
  • A deck repair needs a permit when structural parts are involved or most of the boards are replaced.
  • Only one accessory dwelling unit is allowed per primary home, and the primary home must be owner occupied.
  • Paved parking or other hard surface for a single-family house generally may not exceed 35% of the front yard.

A rezoning, special use permit or variance is a slower road. Staff require a pre-application meeting, the process runs about two months, and the department accepts only four such applications a month. If a buyer's plan depends on a zoning change, that timeline belongs in your price conversation.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and city fees work on a Mulberry house?
sections.html:
Gwinnett County's tax commissioner bills the property. The commissioner's 2026 guide says a Mulberry bill carries local Mulberry solid waste and stormwater fees, and the office's city-tax page says it also collects special assessments for the city. Ask the tax commissioner at 770-822-8800 to walk through every line on your parcel before you list.

Gwinnett says bills usually go out in August or September and fall due in October or November. A late balance picks up 0.81% interest each month, plus a 5% penalty after 120 days and another 5% after each further 120 days, capped at 20%. The office accepts partial payments as long as the balance is cleared by the due date, and it does not send bills to mortgage companies, so an escrow customer should confirm the lender paid.

Three Gwinnett rules matter to a seller. A homestead exemption requires that you owned and lived in the home on January 1, and an application should reach the county by the appeal deadline printed on the assessment notice. An assessment appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date. For 2026 the state's one-time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant was applied to bills for eligible homestead owners.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax bill when a Mulberry house sells?
sections.html:
The person who owned the house on January 1 owes the full year, and Gwinnett sends a bill to both the old and new owner when a sale happens later in the year. If the bill goes unpaid, the lien is filed against the January 1 owner unless three things are in place within 90 days of the due date:

  • The buyer's assumption of the tax liability is documented with acceptable proof.
  • The deed is in the new owner's name.
  • The deed has been properly recorded.

The commissioner publishes sample contract wording. A line such as "Payment of all outstanding taxes and assessments not paid at settlement and those incurred in the future are assumed by purchaser" counts as acceptable. A line saying the parties "agree to adjust the pro-rations amongst themselves" does not. Ask your closing attorney to use the acceptable style, and keep a copy of the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a Mulberry property in Georgia?
sections.html: Georgia charges a real estate transfer tax of $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100. The seller is liable by law, though contracts often assign it to the buyer, and it must be paid before the clerk of superior court records the deed. The closing attorney files the PT-61 declaration electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. Ask the Gwinnett clerk of superior court for the current recording fee schedule.

sections.h2: What should I fix before listing a Mulberry house?
sections.html:
Start with what a code officer or inspector would flag from the street. Mulberry's code enforcement page lists grass and weeds over 12 inches, inoperable vehicles without current tags, and yard trimmings left on a public street or sidewalk. Front-yard soil should be covered by grass, ground cover or other landscaping.

Next, collect permit records for any addition, deck, pool or fence. Pools need a permit and an approved location plan, fences need an approved application, and the city asks owners to call 770-341-9640 before removing trees because a limited land disturbance permit may apply. Gaps in the permit record can come up during a buyer's inspection, so sort them out before the house is listed.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell on my own, or take a cash offer in Mulberry?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent usually reaches the most buyers and takes the longest, because you pay for showings, repair requests and agent commissions. Selling on your own saves the commission but leaves pricing, contracts and disclosures to you. A cash investor buys as-is and can close on a short timeline, and the trade is a price set by what the buyer must spend on repairs and resale.

Whichever route you take, get at least two written offers or price opinions, read the contract for who pays transfer tax and closing costs, and have a Georgia closing attorney handle the deed. If the house has unpermitted work, an expired permit or a tax balance, disclose it early. Offers that survive that disclosure are the ones worth acting on.

faqs.q: Is Mulberry, GA a real city?
faqs.a: Yes. The Census Bureau lists Mulberry city with 41,445 residents as of July 1, 2025, and Gwinnett County's notice says the city handles planning, zoning, code enforcement and permitting inside its limits since January 1, 2025. The same notice mentions court cases over the charter, so confirm anything permit-related with Mulberry staff at 770-341-9640.

faqs.q: Do I get permits from Gwinnett County or from Mulberry?
faqs.a: Inside Mulberry limits, permits go through the city's SagesGov portal. Gwinnett County still performs plan review and inspections for fire, water and sewer. Use the city's address lookup if you are unsure whether your parcel is inside the limits.

faqs.q: Will I still get a property tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, if you owned the house on January 1. Both seller and buyer receive a Gwinnett bill, and the January 1 owner stays responsible unless acceptable proof of the buyer's assumption, the new deed and the recording are all in place within 90 days of the due date. Your closing attorney should include assumption language in the contract.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Gwinnett assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the annual assessment notice. Appeals can be filed online, in person or by mail, and a homestead application for the current year should also arrive by that deadline. Call the assessors at 770-822-7200 with questions.

faqs.q: What does Georgia charge to transfer a house I sell in Mulberry?
faqs.a: The state transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100 of the sale price. The seller owes it by law, and many contracts shift it to the buyer. It is collected when the deed is recorded with the clerk of superior court.
